records.reason: Methylquinoline at 10/1 has extreme predicted V1/V2 widths; tests transfer of the severe quinoline late-elution error seen in e47aebe2660b9e1528de and 23ef03f3e75e40b20095.
The 5/1 methylquinoline point extends the same heteroaromatic response curve into a high-width regime, linking to the quinoline failures e47aebe2660b9e1528de and 33ffc69a253a89f15995.
Methylquinoline at 2/1 provides an intermediate solvent-strength point to determine whether its predicted slope is smooth or sharply nonlinear.
The 1/1 methylquinoline point anchors the early part of the response curve and tests whether the large 5/1 to 10/1 widths collapse at weaker eluent.
Quinoline at 10/1 with a higher loading volume is a high-width loading/condition contrast to e47aebe2660b9e1528de and directly probes persistent late-elution underprediction.

Quinoline at 1/1 tests whether the model recovers a compact early-elution regime before the large widths seen at stronger PE/EA ratios.
A zero-EA point for the amino ester tests the lower endpoint of a response curve whose 20/1 labels had V2 errors of -54.2 and -51.8 mL in 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 and 5d6d4ac0c1dfacbde53d.
The 1/1 amino-ester point fills a missing low-strength condition and tests whether the abrupt predicted V2 expansion is chemically plausible.
The 2/1 amino-ester point probes the transition into the broad-width region, helping distinguish smooth solvent response from a model artifact.
The 5/1 amino-ester point provides a mid-strength label for repairing the systematic V2 underprediction observed in 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 and 5d6d4ac0c1dfacbde53d.
At 10/1, this amino ester tests extrapolation toward the previously measured 20/1 failure region while retaining the same scaffold.
This 20/1 PE-loaded amino-ester condition is a loading-solvent contrast to the measured DCM pair 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 and 5d6d4ac0c1dfacbde53d.
A low-loading 2/1 point for the highly oxygenated diester tests loading sensitivity in the same multi-acceptor region as ca467c94f14b2219503e and 9e3f598e00375ec93d9b.
The matched higher-loading 2/1 diester condition isolates loading amount from 74ce463c8423fbd22dc4 while targeting the large V2 residual family ca467c94f14b2219503e and 9e3f598e00375ec93d9b.
The 1/1 diester point extends the solvent-response curve into weaker eluent and tests whether the model's broad tail contracts monotonically.
A zero-EA diester label provides a compact-tail endpoint for comparison with the severe measured V2 underpredictions in ca467c94f14b2219503e and 5d530b2f228ed39ff952.
Nitrobenzaldehyde at 10/1 probes a polar acceptor-rich scaffold at high predicted width, extending the mixed nitro errors in a5f9179bfb146ad70953 and b6f1b33a5491968c645e.
The 20/1 nitrobenzaldehyde condition tests the stronger-eluent end of the polar response and whether V1/V2 remain systematically overpredicted.
At 2/1 this nitrobenzaldehyde point supplies an intermediate condition for identifying nonlinear polar retention behavior.
The 1/1 nitrobenzaldehyde point anchors the early regime and contrasts with the late measured values of a5f9179bfb146ad70953 and b6f1b33a5491968c645e.
A 20/1 trifluoromethoxy phenol label tests donor-assisted silica retention and high-width V2 behavior related to 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf and c45057c2cab40f4fa2be.
The 10/1 phenol condition fills the mid-strength response curve for a donor-containing aromatic with the same functional-group arrangement as the prior high-error example 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf.
At 5/1, this phenol tests whether predicted tail widths contract smoothly before the stronger-eluent regime.
The 2/1 phenol point adds a lower-strength condition to distinguish donor effects from ordinary solvent-strength dependence.
Dimethyl benzophenone at 1/1 provides an early endpoint for a bulky aromatic response curve, addressing the dibenzoylbenzene failure 0c5c35afb3a24375c153 by chemical analogy.
The 10/1 point tests solvent sensitivity of a bulky hydrophobic ketone in a region related to the large residuals of 0c5c35afb3a24375c153 and 1395836aef00d6a880b0.
The 20/1 dimethyl benzophenone condition probes the predicted V2 expansion before the strongest eluent and supplies a middle response point.
The 50/1 point tests the strong-eluent tail of the same bulky aromatic scaffold, directly targeting model extrapolation beyond the measured failure 0c5c35afb3a24375c153.
High-loading nitrobenzophenone at 50/1 targets a broad polar V2 prediction and forms a matched loading pair with 4862e2fb71344ce16021.

The lower-loading counterpart to b514312eda7950cdcf1c isolates loading effects in a high-TPSA ketone/nitro scaffold, complementary to measured loading ambiguity in ca467c94f14b2219503e and 9e3f598e00375ec93d9b.
Nitrobenzophenone at 20/1 adds a weaker-eluent condition to test whether the high predicted V2 tail changes monotonically with PE/EA.

hypotheses.content: PE/EA changes produce nonlinear, molecule-specific V1/V2 response curves that are insufficiently represented by current labels.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Dense condition curves let the retrained model learn solvent-strength derivatives and identify abrupt transitions rather than relying on descriptor-only interpolation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected heteroaromatic, amino-ester, nitro, phenol, and bulky-ketone curves remain monotonic and smooth across PE/EA?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount may perturb retention less than PE/EA, but the effect can be structure-dependent and weakly identified.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading pairs can teach whether density-times-volume should have a stronger interaction with polar and strongly adsorbing structures.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and PE/EA, are V1/V2 shifts reproducible across the selected loading contrasts?

hypotheses.content: Novel polar, multi-heteroatom, or hydrogen-bonding molecules occupy a model failure region with broad and potentially miscalibrated V2 predictions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The batch supplies direct V2 supervision across nitro, ester, amino, and donor-rich scaffolds where historical tails were severely mispredicted.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do new polar labels remain systematically late or early relative to prediction, or does the error depend on functional-group arrangement?

hypotheses.content: Bulky high-LogP aromatics can retain unexpectedly late or condition-sensitive behavior that is not captured by molecular weight and lipophilicity alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A related bulky-ketone response curve tests whether the network learns scaffold-specific silica interactions instead of a simple mass/LogP shortcut.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do bulky benzophenone-like compounds show strong solvent slopes and late V2 tails despite hydrophobic descriptors?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic nitrogen heterocycles show condition-sensitive retention that is not captured solely by LogP or molecular weight.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Methylquinoline and quinoline curves directly expand the strongest existing heteroaromatic failure region and provide cross-scaffold contrasts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do quinoline and methylquinoline retain distinct solvent slopes and loading responses despite similar size and heteroatom count?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes reinforce severe V2 underprediction for quinoline and methylquinoline (e47aebe2660b9e1528de, 23ef03f3e75e40b20095, 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321), while amino esters and oxygen-rich diesters continue to show very large late-tail errors (1b1a9ec85268aa66d327, 5d6d4ac0c1dfacbde53d, ca467c94f14b2219503e, 9e3f598e00375ec93d9b). Loading effects remain unresolved because matched pairs differ substantially in measured V2 without a consistent model response. The new batch therefore emphasizes full condition curves and matched loading contrasts in those failure regions, while retaining bulky aromatic controls related to 0c5c35afb3a24375c153 and 1395836aef00d6a880b0.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments form interpretable local designs rather than isolated extremes: four-point heteroaromatic and bulky-ketone curves, six-point amino-ester coverage, multi-point diester and nitro-aromatic curves, and donor-containing phenol conditions. Matched loading pairs are included where predictions are nearly invariant but prior labels suggest possible structure-dependent loading effects. High-width candidates concentrate supervision where historical V2 errors were largest, while chemically distinct early/low-polarity endpoints help prevent overfitting to one failure family. Together these labels should improve condition-response learning, polar-tail calibration, heteroaromatic representation, and generalization across the Row-distribution.
